Propofol: Pfizer. Propofol is the active component of an intravenous anesthetic used for induction and maintenance of general anesthesia.
In which country did the Hawker Siddeley Harrier take place?
Hawker Siddeley Harrier: United Kingdom. The Hawker Siddeley Harrier is a British jet-powered attack aircraft designed and produced by the British aerospace company Hawker Siddeley.
Who is credited with discovering Meitnerium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Meitnerium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
Who is credited with discovering Allergic rhinitis?
Allergic rhinitis: John Bostock. It is classified as a type I hypersensitivity reaction.
Who is credited with discovering SARS-CoV-2?
SARS-CoV-2: Zhang Jixian. The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
First flown in 1987, this medium-lift helicopter began as a joint UK-Italian venture between Westland and Agusta, and several countries use the nickname 'Merlin' for it — which helicopter is it?
AgustaWestland AW101 is a medium-lift helicopter in military and civil use.
With a wingspan up to 3.3 meters and a weight of 15 kilograms, which South American bird is generally considered the largest bird of prey on Earth, sporting a ruff of white feathers around its neck?
Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
This amino acid carries a guanidino group that serves as the body's precursor for making nitric oxide, and it's encoded by a generous six codons. Which one is it?
Arginine is the amino acid with the formula (H2N)(HN)CN(H)(CH2)3CH(NH2)CO2H.
Only eight species of this stocky-legged, shaggy, short-tailed carnivoran survive, ranging across North and South America and Eurasia — what mammal is it?
Bear are carnivoran mammals of the family Ursidae.

This general medical term describes blood escaping a damaged vessel, whether internally or through a puncture in the skin, with the loss of more than about 15 percent of total volume proving potentially fatal. What is it called?
Bleeding is blood escaping from the circulatory system from damaged blood vessels.

This British dog breed of mastiff type has a stocky build, a large head, thick facial skin folds, and a protruding lower jaw, and is now illegal to breed in the Netherlands over health concerns — name the breed?
Bulldog is a British breed of dog of mastiff type. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.

This quaternary ammonium compound ferries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for energy production, and is concentrated in heart and skeletal muscle, though most people synthesize enough on their own. What is it called?
Carnitine is a quaternary ammonium compound involved in metabolism in most mammals, plants, and some bacteria.
Present naturally in breast milk and added to infant formula, this essential nutrient is also a building block for a neurotransmitter that controls muscle movement — which compound?
Choline is a cation with the chemical formula +.
Named for its snake-like neck (its species epithet means 'snake'), this feisty freshwater reptile has powerful beak-like jaws and ranges from Nova Scotia down to Florida — which species is it?
Common snapping turtle (Chelydra serpentina) is a species of large, freshwater turtles in the family Chelydridae.

This closed sac within the body has a distinct wall of cells that are structurally abnormal compared to surrounding tissue, and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — unlike a pus-filled abscess, what is it called?
Cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.

Derived from the wild rock dove and split into more than 350 distinct breeds, this domesticated bird was already being bred by Mesopotamians more than 5,000 years ago, according to cuneiform tablets — what's the bird?
Domestic pigeon (Columba livia "domestica" or Columba livia forma domestica) is a domesticated bird derived from the rock dove (Columba livia), of which it is also a subspecies.
Psychology, medicine, history, and even computer science all study these pleasure-or-displeasure states, which still lack any agreed scientific definition — what are they?
Emotion are physical and mental states brought on by neurophysiological changes, variously associated with thoughts, feelings, behavioral responses, and a degree of pleasure or displeasure.
Equivalent to one coulomb per volt, this SI unit of electrical capacitance is named after a pioneering English physicist — name the unit?
Farad (symbol: F) is the unit of electrical capacitance, the ability of a body to store an electrical charge, in the International System of Units (SI), equivalent to 1 coulomb per volt (C/V).
Alongside co-founding a file-sharing site, this Swedish entrepreneur also started an internet service provider and web-hosting firm called PRQ — who is he?
Fredrik Neij (born 27 April 1978), alias TiAMO, is the co-founder of The Pirate Bay, and the Swedish Internet service provider and web hosting company PRQ.

Designed at a major tech company in 2007 by Robert Griesemer, Rob Pike, and Ken Thompson, this statically typed, compiled programming language borrows C-like syntax while adding garbage collection and built-in concurrency support — name the language?
Go (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose programming language that is statically typed and compiled.

A spiny mammal with 17 species across five genera in Europe, Asia, and Africa, this creature shares distant ancestry with shrews. There are no native populations in Australia or the Americas, though one extinct genus once roamed North America—what is it?
Hedgehog is a spiny mammal of the subfamily Erinaceinae, in the eulipotyphlan family Erinaceidae.
Petroleum, natural gas, and coal all fall under which class of organic compound built solely from hydrogen and carbon, spanning gases, liquids, waxes, and polymers?
Hydrocarbon is an organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon.

This analytical framework, which arose partly in reaction to both white feminism and the male-dominated Black liberation movement, examines how overlapping social identities create unique combinations of discrimination and privilege — name the concept?
Intersectionality is an analytical framework for understanding how groups' and individuals' social and political identities result in unique combinations of discrimination and privilege.
Court astronomer and advisor to Elizabeth I, this mathematician and alchemist kept one of England's largest libraries and is credited with coining the phrase 'British Empire' — who was he?
John Dee (13 July 1527 - December 1608 or March 1609) was an English mathematician, astronomer, teacher, astrologer, occultist, and alchemist.
Named from the Greek word for 'the hidden one', this colorless, odorless noble gas with atomic number 36 is used in fluorescent lamps and high-powered gas lasers. Name the element?
Krypton (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

This Finnish-American software engineer has led development of a hugely popular open-source operating system kernel since 1991, and also created the distributed version-control system Git — who is he?
Linus Torvalds (born 28 December 1969) is a Finnish and American software engineer who is the creator and lead developer of the Linux kernel since 1991.
This naturally occurring white solid, found as the mineral brucite, has very low water solubility and is a key ingredient in a well-known antacid remedy — what is it?
Magnesium hydroxide is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula Mg(OH)2.
Shaped like a half-moon, this crescent of fibrocartilage partly divides the knee joint and also turns up in the wrist, jaw, and shoulder joints — what is it called?
Meniscus (anatomy) (pl.: menisci or meniscuses) is a crescent-shaped fibrocartilaginous anatomical structure that, in contrast to an articular disc, only partly divides a joint cavity.
Named from a Greek word for lead because its ores were once confused with lead ore, this chemical element bears the symbol Mo and atomic number 42 — name the element?
Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.
A naval aviator who flew the F9F Panther in Korea before commanding Apollo 11, this Ohio-born engineer earned a place in history in 1969 — who is he?
Neil Armstrong (August 5, 1930 - August 25, 2012) was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who, as the commander of the 1969 Apollo 11 mission, became the first person to walk on the Moon.
Many species in this bird family scavenge alongside pigeons and gulls, while two of its city-dwelling members are famous for nesting directly on buildings — which family are they?
Old World sparrow are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Believed to have originated in Sardinia and cultivated since around the 3rd century BC, this flowering herb native to Greece and North Africa is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Parsley (Petroselinum crispum), is a species of flowering plant in the family Apiaceae that is native to Greece, the Balkans, Algeria and Morocco.

Left untreated, this inherited metabolic disorder — caused by a faulty gene needed to break down a certain amino acid — can cause intellectual disability, seizures, and a musty body odor — what is it?
Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inborn error of metabolism that results in decreased metabolism of the amino acid phenylalanine.
This category of polymer includes both natural proteins like wool and silk, and synthetic materials like nylon and aramid fibers — what is it?
Polyamide is a polymer with repeating units linked by amide bonds.

Harvested from the seeds of several Plantago species, this common dietary fiber supplement relieves both constipation and mild diarrhea, and occasionally doubles as a food thickener — what is it called?
Psyllium is the common name used for several members of the plant genus Plantago whose seeds are used commercially for the production of mucilage.
Derived from an Ancient Greek word for 'flow,' this umbrella term covers more than 200 different conditions causing chronic joint or connective-tissue pain, including arthritis — what's the term?
Rheumatism (from the Ancient Greek, rhema) or rheumatic disorders are conditions causing chronic, often intermittent pain affecting the joints or connective tissue.
Which genus of 20 to 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae produces both a fragrant white flower cluster and a dark berry, each with their own distinct common name?

Sambucus is a genus of between 20 and 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae. The various species are commonly referred to as elder, with the flowers as elderflower, and the fruit as elderberry.
Believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso, this toy dog breed originated in Tibet — name the breed?
Shih Tzu is a toy dog or pet dog breed originating from Tibet and believed to be bred from the Pekingese and the Lhasa Apso.

This now-discredited scientific theory held that living creatures like fleas or maggots could regularly arise directly from non-living matter such as dust or rotting flesh, and was coherently synthesized by Aristotle. Name the theory?
Spontaneous generation is a superseded scientific theory that held that living creatures could arise from non-living matter and that such processes were commonplace and regular.
Down, Wolf–Hirschhorn, and Andersen–Tawil are all named examples of this medical term for a cluster of correlated signs and symptoms — what is it?
Syndrome is a set of medical signs and symptoms which are correlated with each other and often associated with a particular disease or disorder.
Known in medical Latin as the pollex, this digit sits outermost on the hand when you stand palms-forward — which body part?
Thumb is the first digit of the hand, next to the index finger.
Developed by Microsoft as open-source software, this programming language adds optional static typing to JavaScript and transpiles back into it — name the language?
TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
Named after the Scottish engineer who improved the Newcomen steam engine in 1776, this SI unit of power equals one joule per second — what is it?
Watt (symbol: W) is the unit of power or radiant flux in the International System of Units (SI), equal to 1 joule per second or 1 kgm2s3.
First synthesized by chemist Alexander Shulgin in 1974, this psychedelic compound produces hallucinogenic effects considered milder than LSD or psilocybin — what is it commonly known as?
2C-B: Psychedelic drug. 2C-B, also known as 4-bromo-2,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine or by names such as Nexus or Erox, is a psychedelic drug of the phenethylamine and 2C families.
Also known as the buckeye or conker tree, this deciduous flowering tree is often confused with the unrelated sweet chestnut — which species?
Aesculus hippocastanum: Species of tree in the soapberry family.
Defined by at least one carbon-carbon triple bond and traditionally nicknamed for its simplest member, ethyne (better known as acetylene) — which class of hydrocarbon is this?
Alkyne: Hydrocarbon compound containing one or more C≡C bonds.
This scientific discipline uses techniques from titration to mass spectrometry to identify unknown compounds and measure exactly how much of each substance is present in a mixture - which field?
Analytical chemistry: Study of the separation, identification, and quantification of matter.
Lacking a tail due to a mutation in the TBXT gene, this superfamily of primates includes gibbons as the 'lesser' branch and humans among the 'great' branch — which animal group?
Ape: Superfamily of primates. The family Hylobatidae, the lesser apes, include four genera and a total of 20 species of gibbon, including the lar gibbon and the siamang, all native to Asia.
Larger than a meteoroid but smaller than a planet, most of these rocky, metallic, or icy bodies orbit between Mars and Jupiter — what are they called?
Asteroid: Minor planet found within the inner Solar System.
Also called Asian sea bass, this catadromous fish is widely distributed from the Middle East across South and Southeast Asia to Oceania — which fish?
Barramundi: Species of fish. The species is widely distributed in the Indo-West Pacific, spanning the waters of the Middle East, South Asia, Southeast Asia, East Asia, and Oceania.
This field covers physiological traits like fingerprints and iris patterns, plus behavioral ones like typing rhythm and gait, all used to identify people — what is it called?
Biometrics: Metrics related to human characteristics.
Certified in Canada in 1998, this large-cabin business jet shares its fuselage cross-section with the Challenger 600 and first flew in 1996 — which jet is it?
Bombardier Global Express: Large cabin business jet. The Bombardier Global Express is a large cabin, long-range business jet designed and manufactured by Bombardier Aviation.

Comprising over 250 species that form small colonies of as few as 50 individuals around a single queen, these fuzzy insects were introduced to New Zealand and Tasmania and can sting repeatedly without dying — which insect is it?
Bumblebee: Genus of insect. A bumblebee (or bumble bee, bumble-bee, or humble-bee) is any of over 250 species in the genus Bombus, part of Apidae, one of the bee families.
Called 'rockmelon' in Australia and 'spanspek' in South Africa, this orange-fleshed true melon goes by yet another name in North America — what fruit is it?
Cantaloupe: Variety of melon. Originally, cantaloup referred to the true cantaloupe or European cantaloupe with non- to slightly netted and often ribbed rind.
Sold under the brand name Rocephin, this injectable third-generation antibiotic treats everything from meningitis to gonorrhea — which drug?
Ceftriaxone: Antibiotic medication. Ceftriaxone, sold under the brand name Rocephin, is a third-generation cephalosporin antibiotic used for the treatment of a number of bacterial infections.
The only member of the onion genus native to both the New World and Old World, this perennial herb has edible leaves and flowers and doubles as a natural insect repellent — what is it?
Chives: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.

First discovered as an atypical antipsychotic, this medication is reserved for schizophrenia patients who haven't responded to two other drugs, and is also used for psychosis linked to Parkinson's disease — what is it?
Clozapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Clozapine, sold under the brand name Clozaril among others, is a psychiatric medication and was the first atypical antipsychotic to be discovered.
These wind-pollinated, cone-bearing evergreens dominated Earth's landscapes throughout the Mesozoic before flowering plants took over — what group of plants is this?
Conifer: Group of seed plants. As of 2025, 94 conifer species are listed as endangered and 30 as critically endangered.
Encompassing roadrunners, koels, and anis among its roughly 150 species, this widespread bird family favors trees but includes some ground-dwellers — what is it?
Cuckoo: Family of birds. The cuckoo family includes the common or European cuckoo, roadrunners, koels, malkohas, couas, coucals, and anis.

This acute medical syndrome develops over hours or days and causes disturbed attention, awareness, and sometimes hallucinations — often triggered by illness, substances, or their withdrawal — what is it called?
Delirium: Severe confusion that develops quickly, and often fluctuates in intensity.
The first species humans ever domesticated — over 14,000 years ago, before farming even began — this descendant of wolves later evolved to thrive on a starchy diet. What is it?
Dog: Domesticated species of canid. The dog (Canis familiaris or Canis lupus familiaris) is a domesticated descendant of wolves.

A British physicist who hauled a captured German thermionic valve back from the Western Front, he won the 1947 Nobel for mapping the ionosphere — work that paved the way for radar and shortwave radio. Who was he?

Native across the arctic and temperate Northern Hemisphere, this fern relative grows both a spore-bearing stem and a separate sterile green one, and is often mistaken for mare's tail — what plant is it?
The only member of its family found outside the Americas, this tiny insect-eating bird holds its short tail erect and is unusually polygynous for a songbird — what is it?
Eurasian wren: Species of bird. In Anglophone Europe, it is commonly known simply as the wren.

Marked by widespread chronic pain plus fatigue and foggy thinking, this condition affects 2 to 4% of people, more often women, and was first recognised in the 1950s but only defined in 1990 — what is it?
Known for wood used in tool handles, electric guitars, and Morgan Motor Company's sports car frames, this tree genus produced nymphs called the Meliae in Greek myth — which genus?
Fraxinus: Genus of plants. The genus is widespread throughout much of Europe, Asia, and North America.
Called 'a bridge between the natural and social sciences,' this discipline studies Earth's lands, features, inhabitants, and how they all came to be — what is it?
Geography: Study of Earth's spatial information.
This Intel co-founder proposed the famous observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years — who is he?
First described in 1893 during a flu pandemic and mistakenly blamed as its cause, this Gram-negative bacterium causes pneumonia and meningitis mainly in infants — which bacterium?
Haemophilus influenzae: Species of bacterium. The bacteria are mesophilic and grow best at temperatures between 35 and 37 °C.

Famous for the ideas of "bounded rationality" and "satisficing," this remarkable scholar won both a Turing Award and a Nobel in Economics — bridging computer science, economics, and psychology. Who was he?
Herbert A. Simon: American academic and Nobel Laureate (1916–2001)

Found only in the Americas from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego, these roughly 375 species pull off rapid, maneuverable flight thanks to an exceptional metabolism — and their males flaunt the widest plumage diversity of any bird — what are they?
Formed by the merger of two hip flexor muscles that join at the femur's lesser trochanter, this is the body's strongest flexor of the hip — what is it called?
Iliopsoas: Joined psoas and iliacus muscles of the hip and thigh.
The largest tree fruit on Earth can hit 120 pounds and 35 inches long — a 'multiple fruit' made of thousands of individual flowers, with a single tree bearing hundreds a year. What is it?
On January 26, 1926, this Scottish inventor gave the world's first demonstration of a working mechanical television system — who is he?
With an average length of 3.18 to 4 meters and a record of 5.85 meters, this snake is the world's longest venomous species, endemic to Asia. What is it?
King cobra: Group of venomous snakes from Asia.
Spread through the bite of sandflies, this parasitic disease can appear in cutaneous, mucocutaneous, or visceral forms, the last marked by fever and an enlarged spleen — what is it called?
Leishmaniasis: Disease caused by parasites of the Leishmania type.

This anatomic form of lung infection causes inflammatory fluid to consolidate across an entire continuous section of one lung, and in children shows up instead as a rounded pattern due to immature air-pore connections — what is it?
Lobar pneumonia: Lung infection. It is one of three anatomic classifications of pneumonia (the other being bronchopneumonia and atypical pneumonia).
A field of artificial intelligence built on statistics and optimization, it develops algorithms that learn from data and handle unseen examples without being explicitly programmed — what is it?
Machine learning: Subset of artificial intelligence. Statistics and mathematical optimisation methods compose the foundations of machine learning.

In 1835 this Scottish polymath and Caroline Herschel became the first female Honorary Members of the Royal Astronomical Society, and she signed first on John Stuart Mill's 1866 petition for women's suffrage — who was she?
Patented in 1922 and later marketed as Novalgin or Analgin, this painkiller's sale is restricted in some countries due to a rare blood-cell risk called agranulocytosis — what is it?
Metamizole: Medication. Metamizole or dipyrone is a painkiller, spasm reliever, and fever reliever drug.
Cultivated by the Aztecs and named partly for a Mexican state capital, this flower opens each evening between four and eight o'clock and perfumes the night before closing by morning — which plant?

Mirabilis jalapa: Species of flower. Mirabilis jalapa, the marvel of Peru or four o'clock flower, is the most commonly grown ornamental species of Mirabilis plant, and is available in a range of colors.
Serving as Turkey's minister overseeing environment and climate, who is set to preside over the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, COP31?
A healthy kidney contains up to 1.5 million of these microscopic filtering units, each pairing a capillary tuft with a cup-shaped capsule — what is it called?
Nephron: Microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney.
Represented by symbols like '11' in the Hindu-Arabic system used worldwide, these mathematical objects serve to count, measure, and label — what are they called?
Number: Used to count, measure, and label. The most basic examples are the natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so forth.
Described as far back as the 300s BC by Hippocrates, this bone infection most often strikes the spine in adults and the long bones in children — which condition?
Osteomyelitis: Infection of the bones. It may be acute or chronic and can be classified as hematogenous or non-hematogenous.
Also known as trisomy 13, this chromosomal condition arises when cells carry extra genetic material from chromosome 13, causing widespread organ defects — which syndrome?
Patau syndrome: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 13.
Named from the Greek word for 'apparition' due to their leaf-like camouflage, this insect order includes stick insects and leaf insects. What's it called?
Phasmatodea: Order of stick and leaf insects.
Members of this eukaryotic kingdom mostly make their own food with chlorophyll, though parasitic kinds have ditched photosynthesis entirely to feed off others — what kingdom is it?
Plant: Kingdom of organisms. Historically, as in Aristotle's biology, the plant kingdom encompassed all living things that were not animals, and included algae and fungi.
This corticosteroid treats conditions from rheumatoid arthritis to asthma but can cause bone loss and psychiatric side effects with long-term use — what is it called?
Prednisolone: Corticosteroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a vein, used topically as a skin cream, or as eye drops.
Often starting as a blood clot in the leg that travels to the lungs, this blockage can cause chest pain on breathing in, coughing up blood, and sudden death — what is the condition?

Pulmonary embolism: Blockage of an artery in the lungs. Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a blockage of an artery in the lungs by a substance that has moved from elsewhere in the body through the bloodstream (embolism).

Native to the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China, this small mammal sports dense reddish-brown fur, a ringed tail, and curved semi-retractile claws for climbing — and was the original bearer of its famous name. What is it?
Red panda: Species of mammal in Asia.
First created in 1994 near Darmstadt, Germany, this extremely radioactive synthetic element is named for the physicist who discovered X-rays — which element is it?
Roentgenium: Chemical element with atomic number 111 (Rg)
This Taiwanese-American physicist shared the 1976 Nobel Prize with Burton Richter for discovering the subatomic J/ψ particle. Who is he?
Samuel C. C. Ting: Nobel prize winning physicist.
Coined by Horace Walpole in 1754, this term for a lucky accidental discovery describes how penicillin, Post-it Notes, and the microwave oven all came about — what is it?

Thanks to extra joints in its skull, this legless, scale-covered reptile can swallow prey far bigger than its own head — and its paired organs sit one behind the other to fit a narrow body. What creature is it?
Working largely in isolation, this early-20th-century Indian mathematician solved problems thought unsolvable, though leading professionals first dismissed his work as too novel — who was he?
Occurring in our galaxy roughly once every 61 years, though the last confirmed sighting was back in 1604, this luminous stellar explosion can briefly outshine an entire galaxy?
Encompassing everything from the electrical telegraph to modern radio, this field is defined as the transmission of information over distance using electrical or electronic means — what field is it?
Telecommunications: Transmission of information electromagnetically. The physical limitations of metallic media prompted the development of optical fibre.
This blood-feeding arachnid's oldest fossils date back roughly 100 million years to the Cretaceous, and it comes in two main flavors: hard-bodied and soft-bodied — which parasite?
Tick: Order of arachnids in the arthropod phylum.

This genetic disorder causes small body size, heart defects, clenched fists with overlapping fingers, and severe intellectual disability, with risk rising alongside maternal age. What's the condition?
Trisomy 18: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 18.
This Soviet chemist led efforts to contain the 1986 Chernobyl disaster and later briefed the international community in Vienna, though he omitted key design flaws in the reactor. Who was he?
Valery Legasov: Former Soviet inorganic chemist and member of the USSR Academy of Sciences (1936–1988)
Also known as ash pumpkin or winter melon, this South and Southeast Asian plant is grown for its very large fruit, eaten as a vegetable once mature — which plant?
Wax gourd: Species of vine and edible fruit.
Known to TV audiences as 'Dr. Now,' this Iranian-born American surgeon has spent over a decade helping patients on My 600-lb Life reach life-saving weight loss — who is he?
Younan Nowzaradan: Iranian-American surgeon, television personality, and author (born 1944)
Arsenic is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for arsenic is As. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
What is the chemical symbol for nihonium?
The symbol for nihonium is Nh. Nihonium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Nh and atomic number 113.

In what year was Jesse Plemons born?
Jesse Plemons (born April 2, 1988) is an American actor.

Nick Jonas: Nicholas Jerry Jonas (born September 16, 1992) is an American singer, songwriter, musician and actor.

Nicole Kidman: Nicole Mary Kidman (born 20 June 1967) is an Australian-American actress and producer.

Zac Efron: Zachary David Alexander Efron (born October 18, 1987) is an American actor.
In what year was Andy Warhol born?
Andy Warhol (born Andrew Warhola Jr.; August 6, 1928 – February 22, 1987) was an American artist and filmmaker.
In what year was Meryl Streep born?
Meryl Streep: Mary Louise "Meryl" Streep (born June 22, 1949) is an American actress.
In what year did Sharon Tate die?
Sharon Tate: Sharon Marie Tate Polanski (January 24, 1943 – August 9, 1969) was an American actress and model.

In what year was Argylle first released?
Argylle is a 2024 action-comedy film directed by Matthew Vaughn, and written by Jason Fuchs.
